newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin still has cold, surgeon says no danger.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin still has cold, surgeon says no danger.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin was still at his country residence outside Moscow on Wednesday nursing a cold but the surgeon who gave him a heart bypass two months ago said there was no reason for concern about his health.

"He is staying at Gorky-9 and keeping to the same treatment, being partially confined to bed," a Kremlin spokesman told Reuters. Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov is keeping a close eye on the 65-year-old president.

Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon who led the team that performed a multiple bypass on Yeltsin's coronory arteries on November 5, told Itar-Tass news agency the cold was in no way related to the operation and posed no threat to his heart.
To suggest otherwise was "pure speculation", he said.
Akchurin said that although, in the two or three months after surgery, "it is better to avoid any illness, the president's cold can scarcely cause problems for the heart".
On Monday, Yeltsin cancelled engagements for a few days.
He look tired and pale in television footage of his meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl near Moscow on Saturday.

His chief spokesman said on Monday the president had a caught a heavy cold. Russian media have reported that several of the president's family had fallen victim to a cold epidemic sweeping Moscow over the New Year holiday period.
Texan heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised Akchurin during the heart surgery, said on Monday the president was recovering on schedule.
